about: The steps the kit can't do through the API, for whoever does them (the customer's admin or the SE). Click paths marked verified were seen in a live console (2026-10); the others say what to search for in the console's Search menu, which finds any page by name. Keep the steps short, in order, and say what done looks like.

setup.api_client.title: Create the POV's API client
steps: Sign in to the Zscaler console as an admin.
Go to Administration > API > OneAPI > API Clients and click Add API Client.
Name it as the role spec says (ZPOV <pov-id>), and give it the access the role spec lists for each product: view everywhere in scope, write only where it says full.
Create a client secret and copy it once: the SE types it straight into the console's Connect step (it goes to the SE's keychain).
Send the SE the client ID. Never send the secret by email or chat.
setup.api_client.done: Connect signs in and ticks Connect.

setup.zdx_role.title: Give the API client a ZDX role
steps: Open Administration > API > OneAPI > API Clients and edit the POV's client.
Under its resources or roles, add Digital Experience (ZDX) with a view-only role (the kit only starts deep traces if a use case asks).
Save, then click Check now here (or run Preflight again).
setup.zdx_role.done: Check now says ZDX is readable.

setup.zpa_customer_id.title: Find the ZPA customer ID
steps: In the Zscaler console, open ZPA's Public API page: Configuration & Control > Public API > API Keys (or search the menu for Public API). The customer ID is shown there, and also in the ZPA admin URL.
Copy the Customer ID (a long number, all of it). It isn't a secret.
Paste it into Connect > ZPA customer ID (or `pov-kit set customer_id <number>`), then click Check now here.
setup.zpa_customer_id.done: Check now says ZPA is readable.

zid.ca.entitlement.title: Entitle the POV's pilot group (Internet & SaaS)
zid.ca.entitlement.path: Administration > Subscription > End User Entitlements (Zscaler Help; not in every console version)
steps: In the Zscaler console, search the menu for Entitlement and open the end-user (service) entitlements page. Zscaler Help puts it at Administration > Subscription > End User Entitlements; some consoles place it elsewhere.
Choose Internet & SaaS (and Private Access, with ZPA).
Assign the user group named in the change list (ZPOV - pilot users) and save.
Back in the POV console, click Apply again: it carries on from where it stopped.
zid.ca.entitlement.done: Apply says ZIA sees the group; the kit checks the members' entitlement itself.

zia.ca.entitlement.title: Pilot users are entitled to Internet & SaaS
steps: Only in tenants that entitle chosen users or groups (common with Okta or Entra ID).
Search the console menu for Entitlement, open the end-user (service) entitlements page and choose Internet & SaaS.
Make sure the pilot group (or each pilot user) is assigned, and save.

zid.ca.passwords.title: Set the new pilot users' passwords
steps: Go to Administration > Authentication > Directory > Users.
Open each user the POV created (named ZPOV: ...) and set or reset its password.
Users on a domain your identity provider owns (Okta, Entra ID) can't take a ZIdentity password: the kit puts its own test users on <vanity>.zslogin.net for that reason.
zid.ca.passwords.done: The user signs in to Client Connector.

zia.ca.malware.title: Malware Protection blocks viruses and unwanted apps
steps: Malware Protection is tenant-wide and the customer's, so the kit only reads it.
Search the console menu for Malware Protection.
Check that viruses, unwanted applications, trojans and worms are set to Block (the EICAR test relies on it). Change it only if the customer agrees.
zia.ca.malware.done: The kit's check shows viruses blocked; the probe pack's EICAR test passes.

zcc.ca.devices.title: Pilot devices run Client Connector, signed in as pilot users
steps: In the POV console, Next steps > Set up a pilot device: pick the pilot user and the OS, then copy the one-line command or download the setup script (it has the POV's probe pack inside).
On the device: macOS, paste it into Terminal (approve the settings profile in System Settings when asked); Windows, paste it into PowerShell opened with Run as administrator.

It installs Client Connector for this tenant (cloud, domain and user filled in) from the kit's pinned, signature-checked copy. To use the customer's own version instead, download it from Platform Releases and give it to the setup (--pkg FILE on macOS, -Msi FILE on Windows).
Sign in to Client Connector as the pilot user, then check Internet Security shows On (More > Update Policy if not).
With the setup script, the POV's tests run by themselves once traffic goes through Zscaler; send the results file from the Desktop to the SE.
zcc.ca.devices.done: The kit's check finds each pilot device registered, and the probe results are imported.
zcc.ca.devices.path: Infrastructure > Common Resources > Deployment > Platform Releases (installers; per Zscaler Help)

zcc.by_hand.title: Build the POV's Client Connector profiles by hand
zcc.by_hand.when: when Apply says the API refused them, or there's no default to copy
steps: In the console, search the menu for Forwarding Profile and add one with exactly the name in the change list's spec: ZIA action Tunnel, Z-Tunnel 2.0, on every network type.

Search the menu for App Profiles, open the Windows app profiles and add one with exactly the name in the spec: for the pilot group only, Install Zscaler SSL Certificate on, the forwarding profile from step 1.
Put it above any broader app profile in the order.
In the POV console, Status > Fix drift adopts both by their exact names.
zcc.by_hand.done: Status shows the Client Connector profiles adopted.

casb.ca.tenant.title: Connect a SaaS tenant for SaaS security
casb.ca.tenant.who: customer admin (with the SaaS app's admin)
steps: Search the console menu for SaaS Application Tenants and add one (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Box...).
Sign in with the SaaS app's admin account to grant Zscaler read access (an OAuth consent the kit can't give).
Wait for the first scan to finish, then run the checks again in Preflight.
casb.ca.tenant.done: Preflight shows a connected SaaS tenant.

zpa.ca.connectors.title: Deploy the POV's App Connectors
steps: In the POV console, Next steps > ZPA App Connectors: download the AWS or Azure template and show the provisioning key.
Deploy the template in the customer's cloud account, pasting the key into its ProvisioningKey field (nowhere else).
Wait about ten minutes for both connectors to enroll.
zpa.ca.connectors.done: The kit's check shows 2 POV connectors connected.

zpa.ca.users.title: Pilot users have ZPA turned on in Client Connector
steps: Search the console menu for App Profiles and open the profile the pilot devices use (the POV's own, with Client Connector in the POV).
Make sure Zscaler Private Access is enabled for it (and that the pilot users have the Private Access entitlement).
On a pilot device: Client Connector > More > Update Policy, then check Private Access shows On.
zpa.ca.users.done: The kit's check finds the access rule scoped to the pilot group and the connectors up; a pilot user reaches the POV app.

end.api_clients.title: Delete the POV's API clients
steps: Go to Administration > API > OneAPI > API Clients.
Delete the client(s) named ZPOV <pov-id> (and the read-only one, if Claude Desktop had one).
end.api_clients.done: The kit can no longer sign in to the tenant.
